summary: Iter17 backend-only check of normalized uniqueness in UNIV-2026-BO-01. All 15/15 pytest tests pass. (1) DB fields: there are 1040 ánforas with numero_anfora_normalizado exactly '1'..'1040' and 520 mesas with numero_mesa_normalizado exactly '1'..'520'. All recinto nombre_normalizado values equal strip().casefold() of nombre, all stored values are already trimmed, and there are no duplicates. (2) The partial unique indexes uniq_anfora_norm / uniq_mesa_norm / uniq_recinto_norm_UNIV_2026_BO_01 exist on (id_eleccion, *_normalizado), with unique=true and partialFilterExpression {id_eleccion: EID}. (3) Every acta matches its entity (numero_anfora, ambiente='Mesa N', recinto=nombre), with 0 mismatches. (4) A temporary PUT of '   TEST_Iter17_x_ZZ  ' on one ánfora, one mesa and one recinto (each with linked actas) stored the trimmed value and the casefolded _normalizado. No other field changed. Every linked acta was updated (numero_anfora / ambiente / recinto). Restoring the original value made each document identical to its original and re-propagated to the actas. (5) PUT duplicates that differ only by case, spaces or a tab return 409, and so do POST duplicates for ánfora, mesa and recinto. Snapshots are identical and nothing was inserted. (6) A PUT to a nonexistent id with a duplicate value returns 404 for all three. (7) A full SHA256 snapshot of all actas plus the ánforas, mesas and recintos of the election is identical before and after the run: 1042 actas, 855 esta_bloqueada; estados are 854 bloqueado, 187 borrador, 1 null. No TEST_ residue remains.
critical_code_review_comments: Check-then-insert is still not atomic. The normalized unique index for this election will raise DuplicateKeyError on a race, and that error is not caught, so the client gets a 500 instead of a 409. Wrap the inserts and updates to map DuplicateKeyError to 409.

The normalized unique indexes are only created for elections that run normalizar-identificadores-demo. Other or new elections have only the app-level check. Also, legacy documents without *_normalizado are invisible to that check.

If normalizar-identificadores-demo is re-run after a new ánfora or mesa is created out of creado_en order, sequential update_one calls can collide with the unique indexes mid-loop and leave a partial state. There is no transaction.
Rewriting acta fields (numero_anfora/ambiente/recinto) without an audit trail may be a concern for blocked actas in an electoral context. Consider logging these changes.
seed_data_creation: None. The temporary PUT values were restored within the same test and verified byte-identical.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use test_unicidad_normalizada_iter17.py: it snapshots at runtime and restores its temporary PUTs. Baseline after normalization: 1042 actas, 855 esta_bloqueada; estados are 854 bloqueado, 187 borrador, 1 null. No OCR, uploads or demo loads were invoked.
